a: coldchainOS is an independent, self-funded, open-source project in active development. It is building tools to connect source documents, operating evidence, transparent calculations and reviewable findings behind cold-storage decisions.

q: What does “Does the cold chain pencil?” mean?
a: It asks whether the real estate, refrigeration equipment, energy costs and operating assumptions of a cold-storage decision actually add up, with the evidence and the math visible so people can check them.

No. What exists today is this website, educational calculators, illustrative worked examples, a small sample dataset, draft evaluation cases and a local-only prototype. There are no customers, integrations, measured savings or certifications.
A founder with 30 years of commercial real estate transaction experience and prior national industrial team leadership (founder-reported). The project has no venture capital and no token.

q: Is it open source, and under what license?
a: The code and documentation are in the public GitHub repository under the MIT License. The brand assets (name, wordmark, mark and Bull artwork) and the sample dataset records are not covered by that license.

q: Can I upload confidential documents to the site?
a: No. The public website accepts no uploads. The dev room is a local-only prototype that reads only file names in your browser and sends nothing anywhere.

q: Is the sample dataset real transaction data?
a: No. The published CRE sample records are model-generated training data, not extracted from real transactions. Property and tenant names are synthetic.
